name: Close-to-table attacker
summary: Stands near the table and takes the ball early, on the rise.
howTheyPlay: Hits fast and flat-ish topspin from just behind the end line. Wins by speed and taking time away, not by heavy spin.
watchOuts: Needs very quick feet over short distances
playingAgainst: Vary the length and the spin. Heavy backspin and slow, spinny loops break their rhythm; wide angles pull them off the table.
quizHint: You like being close and quick, and you would rather redirect speed than create it.

name: All-round attacker
summary: Attacks from both wings and can also push, block and change pace.
howTheyPlay: Builds the point with serve, receive and placement, then opens up with topspin when the ball allows it.
playingAgainst: Find the one shot they like least and keep going there. Force them to commit early.
quizHint: You like a bit of everything and you think your way through points.

name: Mid-distance looper
summary: Plays from a step or two back with big, spinny topspin.
howTheyPlay: Uses the whole body to generate heavy topspin and counter-loops. Loves rallies with time to swing.
playingAgainst: Keep the ball short and low, change pace, and play into the body or the elbow so they can't swing freely.
quizHint: You love big swings and long topspin rallies.

name: Penhold attacker
summary: Holds the bat like a pen and attacks, often with a strong forehand.
howTheyPlay: Fast wrist and quick forehand. Modern penholders also use the reverse side for backhand topspin.
playingAgainst: Play long and deep to the backhand, then switch wide to the forehand.
quizHint: You hold the bat like a pen.

name: Attacking chopper (defender)
summary: Stands back and chops the ball with heavy, varied backspin, then attacks loose balls.
howTheyPlay: Returns topspin with backspin chops from distance, changes the amount of spin, and attacks when the opponent gives a weak ball.
playingAgainst: Be patient, vary loop speed and spin, use the middle, and be ready for the sudden attack.
quizHint: You enjoy defending far from the table and frustrating attackers.

name: Close-to-table blocker / pips player
summary: Stays close, blocks and punches, often with pimples on one side.
howTheyPlay: Uses the opponent's pace and spin, changes the ball's spin with pips, and moves the ball around the table.
watchOuts: Has to create pace from nothing
playingAgainst: Give them little pace to use. Slow, spinny loops and pushes, then attack the loose ball.
quizHint: You like to block, redirect and annoy, maybe with pimples.

name: Not sure yet (balanced)
summary: No style chosen yet. The plan builds a solid, even base.
howTheyPlay: Works on every part of the game equally until a style shows up.
watchOuts: Pick a style once you know what you like
playingAgainst: Play your best shots and notice which ones win you points.
quizHint: You are still finding out what you like.
